resources.string: Name, password and bands of the router\'s Wi-Fi
Both with the same name: each device picks its own. 5 GHz is faster and 2.4 GHz reaches farther.
If Wi-Fi at home comes from other devices (extenders, Deco, another router), leave it like this. Otherwise, turn on at least one band.
Anyone nearby can connect, use your internet and see whatever is not encrypted. Give it a password.
Right now each band has a different name or password. When you save, both will use the ones here.
The name is too long: 32 characters at most, fewer with accents or emoji.
The password must be 8 to 63 characters, without accents.
The router did not bring the Wi-Fi back up with the change, so it was left as it was.

resources.string: This phone will be disconnected too. Connect it to “%1$s” within 3 minutes; otherwise the router will put things back as they were.
The network will have no password: anyone nearby will be able to connect.
Nobody will be able to join the router\'s Wi-Fi until you turn a band back on, by cable or through remote access.
It tells the router which channels and how much power the law allows where it is.
The router doesn\'t know which country it is in
Without a country, Wi-Fi uses the most limited channels and power of all, and most of the 5 GHz band can\'t be used.
Each band has a different country. Pick one for both.
The router didn\'t let the app read its list of countries.
Wi-Fi didn\'t come back with that country (its channel may not be allowed there), so it was left as it was.
Wi-Fi restarts: connected devices drop for a few seconds and rejoin on their own.
The 5 GHz band may take over a minute to come back: on some channels the router first listens for radars.
This phone will drop for a moment too. If it doesn\'t rejoin within 3 minutes, the router will leave things as they were.
